zh_summary: Scott Melker分享Grant Cardone表示，華爾街房地產巨頭如Starwood、Blackstone和Goldman被贖回困住，使他的零售資金成為優勢，因為機構被邊緣化。
en_summary: Scott Melker shares Grant Cardone saying Wall Street's real estate giants like Starwood, Blackstone, and Goldman are trapped by redemptions, turning his retail money into an advantage as institutions are sidelined.
text:
Grant Cardone says Wall Street's real estate giants are trapped by redemptions, turning his retail money into an advantage

"I bought through all the cycles, and I have great relationships with the sellers, and they know I'm a closer. They know that my money is different than their money."

"It is basically a dozen to 15, maybe 25 different guys. Big, giant, enormous investment companies. They just trade. Starwood goes to Blackstone, Blackstone goes to Goldman. They're just flipping it to one another."

"All those guys are sidelined. They have redemption issues. They have pension funds saying, I want my money back. It's been 5 years, dude. I'm done."

"The institutions are all kind of trapped right now. And then there's this guy Grant Cardone that was going to retail investors and never went to their well."

"I have this money that was frowned upon that is now like, oh, your money's perfect. It's discretionary. It's really cheap money. I probably have access to the cheapest money in the world."

Weekly KAOS - The AI Crack, the Hot Print, and the Debt Governor

The AI trade finally cracked and bonds rallied into a hot CPI, which reads to me as a growth scare with the Debt Governor on the throttle

Welcome to the Weekly KAOS — UrbanKaoboy’s end-of-week roundup covering Macro and Geopolitics, where I try and tease out the most impactful bits of the week.

Themes of the Week

The AI trade finally started cracking, and what gave it away was the Bond market rallying straight into a hot CPI, which reads to me as a growth scare more than Inflation, with the Debt Governor and not a Fiscal reckoning on the throttle.

This week the Credit market and the Equity market looked at the same company and could not agree on whether it was still breathing. CoreWeave’s five-year CDS blew out to levels implying better-than-even odds of default, while its stock still carries a roughly $35B price tag. That gap is a microcosmic look at the whole AI story, because the buildout has shifted from running on Equity “funny money” to running on Debt, and Debt comes with a governor of real cash interest payments and refinancing risks that Equity does not have.

The rest of the tape rhymed. Semiconductors fell for eight straight sessions, http://Character.AI filed for bankruptcy, and a line of data-center IPOs got pulled, even as September CPI ran hot at 3.7% and the 10-year yield still FELL on the week.
